title: 2 Secrets Hidden Inside the Aston Martin DB5

scenes.text: The most famous car in cinema was not built the way you think. The original script gave Bond's Aston Martin only a smokescreen. The ejector seat was a compressed-air mock-up. The headlights that blind Bond in the film are reflections from a giant mirror. And the car that started it all has been missing since nineteen ninety-seven. Two secrets hidden inside the Aston Martin DB5, with every claim sourced.
scenes.caption: 2 SECRETS HIDDEN INSIDE THE ASTON MARTIN DB5

scenes.text: Our sources are Wikipedia's DB5 page, Top Gear, the James Bond Dossier, the Ecurie article on the Thunderball cars, Carole Nash, NBC News, CNN, Old Cars Weekly, InsideHook, an RM Sotheby's catalogue and a travel-site specification page. They disagree in places, and we show the disagreements. Our own arithmetic is labelled.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA · TOP GEAR · JAMES BOND DOSSIER · ECURIE · CAROLE NASH · NBC · CNN · OLD CARS WEEKLY · INSIDEHOOK · RM SOTHEBY'S · 007TRAVELERS · DISAGREEMENTS SHOWN

scenes.text: Secret one. The Bond Dossier says the initial Goldfinger script gave the DB5 only a smokescreen. The rest, the guns, the slashers, the ejector seat, grew out of the production. Top Gear says production designer Ken Adam sketched the car and discussed it with special effects supervisor John Stears. So the legend started as a single gadget and then multiplied.
scenes.caption: JAMES BOND DOSSIER: INITIAL SCRIPT GAVE THE DB5 ONLY A SMOKESCREEN · TOP GEAR (J. BARLOW, 27 SEP 2021): KEN ADAM SKETCHED THE CAR, DISCUSSED IT WITH SPECIAL EFFECTS SUPERVISOR JOHN STEARS
scenes.chapter: Secret one: the gadgets were smaller than the legend

scenes.text: Where did the ideas come from? Top Gear quotes Adam saying his frustration with parking damage to his own Jaguar influenced the design, including rear guns and bumpers that became like boxing gloves. The Bond Dossier says director Guy Hamilton proposed the revolving number plates after receiving parking tickets. Two gadgets, according to these sources, came from parking trouble.
scenes.caption: TOP GEAR: ADAM'S PARKING-DAMAGE FRUSTRATION WITH HIS JAGUAR INFLUENCED REAR GUNS AND BOXING-GLOVE BUMPERS · BOND DOSSIER: HAMILTON PROPOSED REVOLVING PLATES AFTER PARKING TICKETS

scenes.text: The Bond Dossier says the tyre slashers were inspired by the scythed chariots in Ben-Hur. Carole Nash says Stears took inspiration for the machine guns and the bulletproof rear screen from the wings of a Second World War Spitfire. These are the sources' accounts of inspiration. We have no production notes of our own to confirm them, so we attribute each one.
scenes.caption: BOND DOSSIER: TYRE SLASHERS ← SCYTHED CHARIOTS IN 'BEN-HUR' · CAROLE NASH (26 SEP 2017): GUNS AND REAR SCREEN ← WINGS OF A WWII SPITFIRE · PRODUCTION NOTES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The full gadget list in the Bond Dossier: a homer that tracks a target on a hidden screen, extending front bumpers that Adam designed but were never shown on screen, tyre slashers, a smokescreen, an oil slick, a bulletproof screen, revolving number plates, an ejector seat and front machine guns. By our count, that is nine items, and one of them never appeared in the film.
scenes.caption: BOND DOSSIER: HOMER · EXTENDING BUMPERS (NEVER SHOWN ON SCREEN; ON THE CORGI MODEL) · TYRE SLASHERS · SMOKESCREEN · OIL SLICK · BULLETPROOF SCREEN · REVOLVING PLATES · EJECTOR SEAT · FRONT MACHINE GUNS = 9 (OUR COUNT)

scenes.text: The oil slick had an earlier idea. The Bond Dossier says dropping nails was abandoned because it was too easy to copy. In the film, according to the same article, the oil slick sends a pursuing Mercedes over a cliff, and the smokescreen blinds another Mercedes, which crashes into a tree. We take the article's word for what the film shows.
scenes.caption: BOND DOSSIER: NAILS IDEA DROPPED AS TOO EASY TO COPY · OIL SLICK SENDS A MERCEDES OVER A CLIFF · SMOKESCREEN → MERCEDES HITS A TREE

scenes.text: Now the ejector seat. The Bond Dossier says Adam stated the device came from a jet fighter and was fully functional, though the filming used a compressed-air mock-up. So the seat in the film was not the real thing. Those two statements sit side by side in the article, and we report both. Whether a working seat was ever installed is not settled by our sources.
scenes.caption: BOND DOSSIER: ADAM — THE DEVICE CAME FROM A JET FIGHTER AND WAS FULLY FUNCTIONAL · FILMING USED A COMPRESSED-AIR MOCK-UP · WHETHER A WORKING SEAT WAS EVER FITTED: NOT SETTLED IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The machine guns have their own secret. The Bond Dossier says they fire from behind the headlights, but the lights that blind Bond in the film are reflections from a giant mirror. It is a piece of film trickery rather than a car feature. Top Gear scored the DB5 ten out of ten for gadgets, which is its opinion of the car, not a measurement.
scenes.caption: BOND DOSSIER: GUNS FIRE FROM BEHIND THE HEADLIGHTS; THE 'LIGHTS' THAT BLIND BOND ARE REFLECTIONS FROM A GIANT MIRROR · TOP GEAR SCORE: GADGETS 10/10 (OPINION)

scenes.text: How long did the conversion take? Top Gear says a small team converted the car in six weeks, using pneumatics, hydraulics and acetylene and oxygen tanks. A crew member had to squeeze into the boot to trigger the smoke screen. The Bond Dossier also says Stears tricked out the car over six weeks. Two sources, one figure.
scenes.caption: TOP GEAR: CONVERTED IN SIX WEEKS WITH PNEUMATICS, HYDRAULICS, ACETYLENE AND OXYGEN TANKS; A CREW MEMBER IN THE BOOT TRIGGERED THE SMOKE SCREEN · BOND DOSSIER: STEARS, SIX WEEKS

scenes.text: The Ecurie article lists the gadgets fitted to the first Bond car: hydraulic over-rider rams front and rear, a Browning thirty-calibre machine gun in each front wing, tyre slashers in the wheel hubs, a retractable rear screen, a radar-tracking scope in the dash, dispensers for oil, caltrops and smoke, revolving plates and an ejection system for the passenger seat.
scenes.caption: ECURIE: HYDRAULIC OVER-RIDER RAMS · BROWNING .30 CAL IN EACH FRONT WING · WHEEL-HUB TYRE SLASHERS · RETRACTABLE REAR BULLETPROOF SCREEN · IN-DASH RADAR-TRACKING SCOPE · OIL / CALTROP / SMOKE DISPENSERS · REVOLVING PLATES · PASSENGER-SEAT EJECTION

scenes.text: Ecurie adds two things fitted but not used on screen: a driver's door telephone to MI6 and a hidden weapons compartment under the driver's seat. It also says the first car's gadgets were basic, built only to work for one take. So the legendary car was, in its first form, a film prop designed to work once.
scenes.caption: ECURIE: ALSO FITTED, NOT USED ON SCREEN — DRIVER'S DOOR TELEPHONE TO MI6; HIDDEN WEAPONS COMPARTMENT UNDER THE DRIVER'S SEAT · FIRST CAR'S GADGETS 'BASIC, BUILT ONLY TO WORK FOR ONE TAKE'

scenes.text: Even the Carole Nash article mentions that a stunt car, labelled FMP seven B, had its German ZF gearbox fail during filming in Switzerland, so it was useless for a high-speed chase. The car the film made famous was therefore supported by a stunt car with a broken gearbox. That is one article's account, and the other sources do not repeat it.
scenes.caption: CAROLE NASH: STUNT CAR FMP 7B — ZF GEARBOX FAILED DURING FILMING IN SWITZERLAND · OTHER SOURCES DO NOT REPEAT THIS

scenes.text: Secret two is about the cars themselves. Most people picture one DB5. Wikipedia says four were made for Goldfinger: two used in filming and two for promotion. Ecurie says Eon wanted two near-identical cars, a lightweight stunt car and a car with Stears' gadgetry for interior shots. The number depends on whether you count the Thunderball cars.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: GOLDFINGER — 4 DB5s MADE (2 FILMING, 2 PROMOTION) · ECURIE: EON WANTED 2 NEAR-IDENTICAL CARS (STUNT + GADGET) · COUNT DEPENDS ON WHETHER THUNDERBALL CARS ARE INCLUDED
scenes.chapter: Secret two: which cars were which

scenes.text: The first Bond car was a DB5 prototype, chassis prefix DP slash two sixteen slash one, finished in Snow Shadow Grey, says Ecurie. Wikipedia says it was Dubonnet Red, fitted with gadgets and later stripped. Those descriptions conflict. We show both and do not decide which is right, since neither source gives a photograph or a build sheet.
scenes.caption: ECURIE: DP/216/1 — SNOW SHADOW GREY · WIKIPEDIA: DP/216/1 — DUBONNET RED · BUILD SHEET / PHOTO: NOT IN OUR SOURCES → CONFLICT SHOWN, NOT RESOLVED

scenes.text: Wikipedia says that car later appeared in The Cannonball Run in nineteen eighty-one, and was stolen in nineteen ninety-seven. It says the car was reported missing in twenty twenty-one. Carole Nash says it was stolen in Florida in nineteen ninety-seven, after being stripped of its gadgets and sold, with later owners fitting non-original weaponry. NBC says many believe it was destroyed.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: DP/216/1 IN THE CANNONBALL RUN (1981); STOLEN 1997; REPORTED MISSING 2021 · CAROLE NASH: STOLEN IN FLORIDA 1997 · NBC: 'MANY BELIEVE IT WAS DESTROYED'

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the car has been missing for twenty-nine years as of this year, nineteen ninety-seven to twenty twenty-six. It was the original, the car that Connery drove, if the sources are right about its identity. Whether it is still out there is something no source can tell us, and we will not guess.
scenes.caption: 2026 − 1997 = 29 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CURRENT WHEREABOUTS: UNKNOWN IN ALL OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: A second car adds a twist. Wikipedia says filming car DB5 slash fourteen eighty-six slash R had no gadgets during shooting. Gadgets were added afterwards for promotion, and it sold at RM Auctions in twenty ten for four point six million dollars. Ecurie says it was originally unmodified and had the gadgets added later. So the car many remember as the Bond car was a plain car in the film.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: DB5/1486/R — NO GADGETS DURING SHOOTING; GADGETS ADDED AFTERWARDS FOR PROMOTION; RM AUCTIONS 2010, $4.6 M · ECURIE: 1486/R ORIGINALLY UNMODIFIED, GADGETS ADDED LATER

scenes.text: The price of that sale is itself disputed. Wikipedia and InsideHook say four point six million dollars. NBC News reported two point six million pounds, or four point one million dollars, at RM in London, with an estimate above three and a half million pounds, bought by Harry Yeaggy of Ohio. By our arithmetic, the gap is about eleven percent.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA / INSIDEHOOK: $4.6 M (2010) · NBC: £2.6 M ($4.1 M), EST. > £3.5 M ($5.5 M), BUYER HARRY YEAGGY, RM LONDON · $4.6 M vs $4.1 M = 11% GAP (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: NBC describes the car as silver, first driven by Sean Connery in Goldfinger and also used in Thunderball. It says the car came with a signed photo of Connery in Switzerland and film memorabilia. It also says Yeaggy might display it publicly in a city like Los Angeles or Moscow. Those plans, from 2010, are a statement of intent, not a record of where the car went.
scenes.caption: NBC: SILVER DB5 · SIGNED PHOTO OF CONNERY IN SWITZERLAND · HARRY YEAGGY — POSSIBLE PUBLIC DISPLAY (LOS ANGELES / MOSCOW) · WHERE THE CAR IS TODAY: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Then comes the Thunderball pair. Ecurie says Eon ordered two more DB5s for Thunderball: chassis two thousand eight slash R, the featured car, and two thousand seventeen slash R. Both had Adam's modifications installed by Aston Martin to work repeatedly, and they were sent to the United States, one to each coast, for promotion.
scenes.caption: ECURIE: EON ORDERED 2 MORE DB5s — DB5/2008/R (FEATURED) AND DB5/2017/R · ADAM'S MODIFICATIONS INSTALLED TO WORK REPEATEDLY · SENT TO THE U.S., ONE EAST COAST, ONE WEST

scenes.text: Ecurie says 2017/R was a pace car at Laguna Seca, driven by Jackie Stewart. CNN says the other car was one of two built in nineteen sixty-five for a U.S. tour promoting Thunderball and has had three owners in over fifty years. Old Cars Weekly says the same car, 2008/R, is one of three surviving James Bond DB5s.
scenes.caption: ECURIE: 2017/R — PACE CAR AT LAGUNA SECA DRIVEN BY JACKIE STEWART · CNN: 2008/R — ONE OF 2 BUILT IN 1965 FOR A U.S. THUNDERBALL TOUR; 3 OWNERS IN 50+ YEARS · OLD CARS WEEKLY: ONE OF 3 SURVIVING BOND DB5s

scenes.text: That car's journey: Ecurie says Danjaq, Eon's Swiss financier, offered the cars for sale in nineteen sixty-nine, and Anthony Bamford bought both. B. H. Atchley of the Smokey Mountain Car Museum in Tennessee later bought 2008/R, and displayed it for thirty-five years in a bolted wire-mesh cage, started regularly. RM Auctions offered it in two thousand six.
scenes.caption: ECURIE: DANJAQ SOLD CARS 1969; ANTHONY BAMFORD BOUGHT BOTH; B.H. ATCHLEY (SMOKEY MOUNTAIN CAR MUSEUM, TN) DISPLAYED 2008/R FOR 35 YEARS IN A BOLTED WIRE-MESH CAGE, STARTED REGULARLY; RM AUCTIONS OFFERED IT 2006

scenes.text: Then the restoration. Roos Engineering in Switzerland restored the car, and Ecurie says all thirteen Adam modifications were refurbished. Old Cars Weekly says the gadgetry was shown working at the Monterey presentation in August twenty nineteen. RM Sotheby's sold it for six million three hundred eighty-five thousand dollars. Six parties bid over four and a half minutes.
scenes.caption: ECURIE: ROOS ENGINEERING (SWITZERLAND) — ALL 13 ADAM MODIFICATIONS REFURBISHED · OLD CARS WEEKLY: $6,385,000, RM SOTHEBY'S MONTEREY, AUG 2019; 6 BIDDERS OVER 4.5 MIN; GADGETS SHOWN WORKING

scenes.text: CNN, covering the same sale, gives the pre-sale estimate as four to six million dollars, and the final as six point four. By our arithmetic, the result was sixty percent above the low estimate and about seven percent above the high one. CNN also says the car had a Browning thirty-caliber machine gun in each fender, which matches Ecurie's list.
scenes.caption: CNN: ESTIMATE $4–6 M; SOLD $6.4 M · $6.4 ÷ $4 = +60%; $6.4 ÷ $6 = +6.7% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BROWNING .30 CAL IN EACH FENDER (CONSISTENT WITH ECURIE)

scenes.text: Why does any of this matter? The Bond Dossier says Aston Martin sales reportedly rose almost fifty percent after the film's release. The word reportedly matters: the article does not give the sales figures behind it. Carole Nash adds that the Corgi toy version became the biggest-selling toy of nineteen sixty-four. Neither claim comes with a table of numbers in our sources.
scenes.caption: BOND DOSSIER: ASTON MARTIN SALES 'REPORTEDLY' UP ALMOST 50% AFTER THE FILM · CAROLE NASH: CORGI DB5 = BIGGEST-SELLING TOY OF 1964 · UNDERLYING SALES FIGURES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES
scenes.chapter: What the film did for the car

scenes.text: The road car was real. Wikipedia says 1,059 DB5 coupes and convertibles were built between nineteen sixty-three and nineteen sixty-five, including one hundred twenty-three convertibles. Sixty-five were Vantage coupes, with three Weber carburettors and three hundred twenty-five horsepower. By our arithmetic, the four Goldfinger cars were less than half a percent of the production run.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1,059 BUILT 1963–65 · 123 CONVERTIBLES · 65 VANTAGE COUPÉS (325 BHP) · 4 ÷ 1,059 = 0.38% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The film cars were so unrepresentative that the real DB5 was a gentler machine. Wikipedia lists a four-litre inline six making two hundred eighty-two brake horsepower at fifty-five hundred revs, a top speed of one hundred forty-five miles per hour and zero to sixty in eight seconds. Carole Nash notes the car had electric windows and a magnesium-alloy body, and full leather trim.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 4.0 L I6, 282 BHP @ 5,500, 145 MPH, 0–60 IN 8 S · CAROLE NASH: CHROME WIRE WHEELS, MAGNESIUM-ALLOY BODY, FULL LEATHER TRIM, ELECTRIC WINDOWS

scenes.text: Specs vary by source. Wikipedia gives a kerb weight of fifteen hundred two kilograms and a width of sixteen eighty millimetres. A travel-site specification page gives fourteen sixty-five kilograms and fifteen eighty. Its zero to one hundred is eight point one seconds, against Wikipedia's zero to sixty in eight. These are small differences, but they show how loosely old-car figures are quoted.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1,502 KG, W 1,680 MM, 0–60 MPH 8 S · 007TRAVELERS: 1,465 KG, W 1,580 MM, 0–100 KM/H 8.1 S · DIFFERENCE 37 KG (2.5%) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Power figures vary too. Wikipedia's text says two hundred eighty-two brake horsepower, while it also mentions a net figure of two hundred ten. The 007 Travelers page says one hundred forty-seven miles per hour, per the company, and a writer there notes that carmakers of the era often exaggerated. That is the writer's opinion, but it is a useful caution.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 282 BHP (TEXT); NET 210 BHP ALSO GIVEN · AUTO123 (27 DEC 2011): 147 MPH PER THE COMPANY; WRITER NOTES ERA EXAGGERATION (OPINION) · WIKIPEDIA TOP SPEED 145 MPH

scenes.text: What did a DB5 cost new? The RM Sotheby's catalogue for a nineteen sixty-four car says four thousand one hundred seventy-five pounds at launch. The 007 Travelers page agrees, listing four thousand one hundred seventy-five in nineteen sixty-three. The auto123 article says four thousand two hundred forty-eight pounds. That is a seventy-three pound difference, about one point seven percent, by our arithmetic.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (LONDON 2022, LOT 146) + 007TRAVELERS: £4,175 · AUTO123: £4,248 · DIFFERENCE £73 = 1.7% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WHICH ONE IS RIGHT: NOT SETTLED IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The 007 Travelers page also lists a price of two hundred thousand pounds in two thousand six. By our arithmetic, that is forty-eight times the launch price of four thousand one hundred seventy-five. Then the Hagerty guide, in April twenty twenty-five, shows six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollars with a ten point two percent rise over the period. That page does not say which condition the figure is for.
scenes.caption: 007TRAVELERS: £200,000 (2006) · £200,000 ÷ £4,175 = 47.9× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · HAGERTY (APR 2025): $659,000, +10.2% (07/24–APR 2025); CONDITION NOT LABELLED; SAME PAGE ALSO CITES ~$860,667 FOR A GOOD-CONDITION AVERAGE-SPEC CAR

scenes.text: And the Top Gear piece from September twenty twenty-one says a fully restored DB5 is worth about a million dollars. The auto123 article in twenty eleven said a good used DB5 was close to two hundred fifty thousand dollars. By our arithmetic, that is a four-fold rise between those two statements, though they come from different outlets and describe cars of different condition.
scenes.caption: TOP GEAR (2021): FULLY RESTORED ~ $1 M · AUTO123 (2011): GOOD USED ~ $250,000 · $1 M ÷ $250,000 = 4× (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT OUTLETS AND CONDITIONS)

scenes.text: The newest film connection is No Time to Die. Wikipedia says eight replica stunt cars were built for it, and one stunt car sold for two point nine two million pounds at a twenty twenty-two charity auction. That is a car built for a film in the twenty-first century, selling for more than most original DB5s, by our reading of the figures above.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: NO TIME TO DIE — 8 REPLICA STUNT CARS; ONE SOLD £2.92 M AT A 2022 CHARITY AUCTION · 'MORE THAN MOST ORIGINAL DB5s' = OUR COMPARISON WITH THE HAGERTY $659,000 FIGURE

scenes.text: There is also the continuation series. Wikipedia says Aston Martin built twenty-five Goldfinger-themed cars, with the first off the line in early July twenty twenty, at an intended price of about two point seven five million pounds. The continuation cars use two hundred ninety brake horsepower, according to Wikipedia. We could not find more detail on the series, so we stop there.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 25 GOLDFINGER-THEMED CONTINUATION CARS · FIRST OFF THE LINE EARLY JULY 2020 · ~£2.75 M EACH · 290 BHP · FURTHER DETAIL: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: One more auction. InsideHook, in June twenty eighteen, wrote about the GoldenEye DB5 headed to Bonhams at Goodwood, with an expert's projection of three to five million dollars. The article says that car sold in two thousand one for two hundred ten thousand six hundred dollars, then a record. By our arithmetic, that is a rise of more than thirteen to twenty-three times, depending on the final price.
scenes.caption: INSIDEHOOK (15 JUN 2018): GOLDENEYE DB5 AT BONHAMS (GOODWOOD) — EXPERT PROJECTION $3–5 M; 2001 SALE $210,600 · $3 M ÷ $210,600 = 14.2×; $5 M ÷ $210,600 = 23.7× (OUR ARITHMETIC; FINAL 2018 PRICE NOT IN OUR SOURCES)

scenes.text: Not every DB5 is a movie car, and the ordinary ones have their own records. RM Sotheby's London catalogued a nineteen sixty-four DB5, chassis fourteen oh six slash R, built on the twenty-first of January and dispatched on the seventh of February nineteen sixty-four. It was restored in twenty fifteen and twenty sixteen by specialists Pugsley and Lewis, with a bare-metal respray in Goodwood Green.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S LONDON 2022, LOT 146: DB5/1406/R · BUILT 21 JAN 1964 · DISPATCHED 7 FEB 1964 · RESTORED 2015–16 BY PUGSLEY AND LEWIS · BARE-METAL RESPRAY IN GOODWOOD GREEN
scenes.chapter: Ordinary DB5s and what they sell for

scenes.text: The catalogue says the matching-numbers six-cylinder engine was rebuilt, along with the rear axle, and the interior retrimmed in tan leather. Later work at Clayton Classics added a high-output alternator, LED headlamps, electronic ignition and a twin-evaporator air-conditioning system. So an ordinary restored DB5 can carry modern conveniences that the factory never fitted.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S LOT 146: ENGINE + REAR AXLE REBUILT · TAN LEATHER RETRIM · CLAYTON CLASSICS — HIGH-OUTPUT ALTERNATOR, LED HEADLAMPS, ELECTRONIC IGNITION, TWIN-EVAPORATOR A/C

scenes.text: The estimate was six hundred twenty-five to six hundred seventy-five thousand pounds, or eight hundred fifty to nine hundred thousand dollars, and the car is listed as not sold. By our arithmetic, the midpoint of the estimate is six hundred fifty thousand pounds, close to the Hagerty guide's six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollars, though one is pounds and the other dollars.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S LOT 146: ESTIMATE £625,000–675,000 ($850,000–900,000); NOT SOLD · MIDPOINT £650,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · HAGERTY APR 2025: $659,000 — DIFFERENT CURRENCIES, NOT A LIKE-FOR-LIKE COMPARISON

scenes.text: The same catalogue says the car was owned by Prince Sadruddin Aga Khan, who bought it in nineteen eighty-eight and kept it about ten years. It also says an export licence is required if the car leaves the UK. Provenance and paperwork, in other words, are part of what a buyer pays for, and part of what limits who can buy.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S LOT 146: PRINCE SADRUDDIN AGA KHAN OWNED IT FROM 1988 FOR ABOUT 10 YEARS · EXPORT LICENCE REQUIRED IF IT LEAVES THE UK · 'WHAT A BUYER PAYS FOR' = OUR READING

scenes.text: Then the rare body styles. Wikipedia says there was one factory shooting brake prototype for David Brown, and eleven or twelve coupes modified by Harold Radford, with the infobox listing thirteen. The Monterey nineteen sixty-five shooting brake sold for one point seven six five million dollars, against an estimate of one to one point four million, according to Old Cars Weekly.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1 FACTORY PROTOTYPE + 11 OR 12 RADFORD CONVERSIONS (INFOBOX: 13) · OLD CARS WEEKLY: MONTEREY 2019 — $1,765,000 vs ESTIMATE $1–1.4 M; ONE OF 12; 3 PRIVATE OWNERS; RECORD FOR A SHOOTING-BRAKE BODY

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the shooting brake beat the top of its estimate by about twenty-six percent. And it sold for roughly two and three-quarter times the Hagerty figure for a standard DB5. The page that quotes the Hagerty price does not give the condition, so this is only a rough scale. Rarity, not just the badge, drives these prices.
scenes.caption: $1.765 M ÷ $1.4 M = +26.1% · $1.765 M ÷ $659,000 = 2.7× (OUR ARITHMETIC; HAGERTY CONDITION NOT LABELLED)

scenes.text: There is also the cost of getting one right. Wikipedia mentions a nineteen sixty-five Vantage restored over three years and two and a half thousand hours at a cost of four hundred thousand pounds. It was bought second-hand for nine hundred pounds in nineteen seventy-three. By our arithmetic, that is one hundred sixty pounds for every hour of work.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1965 VANTAGE RESTORED OVER 3 YEARS, 2,500 HOURS, £400,000 · BOUGHT 1973 FOR £900 · £400,000 ÷ 2,500 = £160/HR (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ESTIMATED VALUE AFTER RESTORATION £1 M

scenes.text: By our arithmetic again, the restoration cost was four hundred forty-four times the purchase price of nine hundred pounds, and the post-restoration estimate of one million pounds is about eleven hundred times the original purchase price. Those are striking ratios, but they combine costs and values from different decades, so treat them as curiosities.
scenes.caption: £400,000 ÷ £900 = 444× · £1,000,000 ÷ £900 = 1,111× (OUR ARITHMETIC; 1973 PRICE vs RECENT COST AND ESTIMATE — NOT INFLATION-ADJUSTED)

scenes.text: Let us line up the film cars by what the sources say. The first gadget car, missing since nineteen ninety-seven. The plain filming car, sold in twenty ten for four point six million dollars. The Thunderball promotional car, sold in twenty nineteen for six point four. And the stunt replica from the latest film, sold in twenty twenty-two for two point nine two million pounds.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA / CNN / OLD CARS WEEKLY: DP/216/1 MISSING SINCE 1997 · 1486/R $4.6 M (2010) · 2008/R $6.385 M (2019) · NTTD STUNT CAR £2.92 M (2022)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the nineteen sixty-five car's price was thirty-nine percent above the two thousand ten sale, in nominal dollars. Nine years separated them. Adjusting for inflation is beyond what our sources provide, so we leave the figure nominal. The cars also differ: one was modified after filming, the other was built with its gadgets from new.
scenes.caption: $6.385 M ÷ $4.6 M = 1.39 → +38.8% (OUR ARITHMETIC; NOMINAL DOLLARS; 2010 → 2019 = 9 YEARS) · INFLATION DATA: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · 2008/R GADGETS FROM NEW; 1486/R ADDED LATER (ECURIE; OLD CARS WEEKLY)

scenes.text: A last comparison with the standard car. Six point three eight five million dollars divided by the Hagerty figure of six hundred fifty-nine thousand is about nine point seven. By our arithmetic, the Bond provenance was worth roughly nine and a half standard DB5s in that comparison. The Hagerty condition is unlabelled, so this is only a rough multiple.
scenes.caption: $6.385 M ÷ $659,000 = 9.7× (OUR ARITHMETIC; HAGERTY CONDITION UNLABELLED; DIFFERENT YEARS 2019 vs 2025)

scenes.text: The chase scenes were shot over about five months. Top Gear says the night-time chase filming began on the ninth of March nineteen sixty-four at Black Park, next to Pinewood, and Connery's last scene was shot there on the twenty-first of July. The last pick-up shots were filmed on the twelfth of August, the day Ian Fleming died.
scenes.caption: TOP GEAR: CHASE FILMING BEGAN 9 MAR 1964 (BLACK PARK, 500 ACRES NEXT TO PINEWOOD) · CONNERY'S LAST SCENE 21 JULY · LAST PICK-UPS 12 AUG 1964, THE DAY FLEMING DIED · 9 MAR → 12 AUG ≈ 5 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: What is missing. The whereabouts of the first gadget car. A reconciled colour for it. The exact cost of building the gadgets. The final price of the GoldenEye car. A reconciled launch price. A neutral, dated source for the almost fifty percent sales claim. If you hold a primary document for any of these, add it in the comments and we will credit it.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: WHEREABOUTS OF DP/216/1 · COLOUR CONFLICT · GADGET BUILD COST · GOLDENEYE CAR FINAL PRICE · LAUNCH PRICE (£4,175 vs £4,248) · SOURCE FOR ~50% SALES RISE
scenes.chapter: What the sources do not say

scenes.text: So the two secrets are these. The gadgets began as a single smokescreen and grew through the production, with some of the most famous tricks done by mirror and compressed air. And the car you picture is several different cars, one of them missing for twenty-nine years. In the other videos this week we compare the DB5 with the DB12, count its cost, and tell the Bond story.
